title: Did Jensen Huang Fool Everyone? A Black Swan Looms and This Year’s Biggest AI Stock Surprise Isn’t TSMC
text:

What if the biggest risk to the AI boom isn’t an AI bubble at all?

Former UBS semiconductor analyst Jonah Cheng, better known as “Captain,” sees a very different black swan approaching: the U.S. midterm elections in November.

In his latest interview, Cheng explains why CSPs are still racing to buy GPUs even as inventories hit record highs—and why a power shortage could eventually turn that buildup into a painful correction.

He also challenges one of the industry’s hottest narratives. While Google and others push toward massive 7×, 8× and 9× reticle-size packages, Nvidia has stopped at 5.5×. Did Jensen Huang’s Rubin Ultra roadmap send everyone chasing the wrong target?

Then there is MediaTek. Cheng argues that its real value in Google’s TPU supply chain isn’t low-margin design services, but something Google cannot easily replicate: SerDes IP.

And his biggest AI surprise of 2026 isn’t TSMC.

It’s Largan Precision—a company few expected to emerge as a serious player in optical communications.

Three unexpected calls. One interview with “Captain.”
